newsitem.title: USA: California to make tobacco suit announcement.
newsitem.headline: California to make tobacco suit announcement.

text.p: California state Attorney General Dan Lungren said Thursday he would shortly make a "major announcement" regarding California's involvement in legal actions against the tobacco industry.
His office declined to comment further.
Lungren, a Republican, said he would make the announcement within an hour in Los Angeles.

California, the most populous state with potentially billions of dollars in claims, has so far not sued major tobacco companies. But pressure has been building in recent weeks on state lawmakers to join the legal battle.

Liggett Group, owned by Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group Ltd , broke ranks in March with other tobacco companies by agreeing to settle with 22 state attorneys general who sued the industry to recoup smoking-related health care costs.
Lungren has long maintained that state litigation would likely fail because of a controversial 1987 state law shielding tobacco companies from product liability claims.
But last month, a spokesman for Lungren said California would likely join other states in suing the major tobacco companies if the state legislature removes the legal barriers.

Earlier this week, state Assembly Speaker Cruz Bustamante, a Democrat, introduced legislation in response to the Liggett accord that would clarify existing state law to remove any barriers that prevent Lungren from suing tobacco companies.
Earlier this year, the state legislature passed nonbinding resolutions calling on Lungren to sue major tobacco companies.
A dozen California counties, including San Francisco, have filed lawsuits in federal and state court against the tobacco companies.
